title: Best Double Strollers 2026: Tandem and Side-by-Side Picks for Real Families
description: Top double strollers of 2026 for two kids — tandem and side-by-side designs tested for fit, fold, and daily usability. Honest picks for every age gap.
lede: A double stroller is one of the most consequential purchases of the two-kid household — the wrong one won't fit through doorways, won't fold into your trunk, or will destroy your wrists on daily walks. We evaluated five models across tandem and side-by-side configurations, with real attention to how they perform for both a newborn-plus-toddler setup and same-age twins.
methodology: Each stroller was pushed through standard doorways (32 inches), loaded into a RAV4 and Odyssey trunk, and evaluated with one child aged 0-6 months and one aged 18 months. Fold complexity, push quality, and canopy coverage were rated.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Double Stroller
paragraphs: The configuration question — tandem (front/back) vs side-by-side — should be your first decision, because it determines everything else. Tandem strollers fit through doorways; side-by-sides don't at standard 30-inch widths unless you specifically check the measurements.

subsections.heading: Tandem vs Side-by-Side
paragraphs: Tandem strollers fit through standard 32-inch doorways and feel more like pushing a single stroller. Side-by-sides give both children equal legroom and sightlines but typically run 28-32 inches wide, which means tight fits at stores, restaurants, and most home doorways. Side-by-sides are generally better for same-age twins; tandems for age-gap families.

subsections.heading: Age Gap Considerations
paragraphs: If you have a newborn and a toddler, you need a seat that fully reclines for the infant (flat or near-flat) plus a standard seat for the older child. Several tandems accommodate an infant car seat in the front or back seat, which buys you the first 12 months without buying a separate infant pram.

subsections.heading: Doorway Width and Urban Use
paragraphs: Measure your front door, your frequently-visited grocery store aisles, and any public transit turnstiles before buying. A 30-inch-wide stroller that doesn't fit through your 28-inch bathroom hallway is going to live in the garage. Most tandems are 20-24 inches wide; most side-by-sides are 28-32 inches.

subsections.heading: Weight and Fold for Car Trunks
paragraphs: Double strollers range from 20 lbs (lightweight tandem) to 35+ lbs (full-featured side-by-side). The fold complexity matters as much as weight — a 25 lb stroller that folds in two seconds beats a 22 lb stroller that requires removing a seat to fit in the trunk.

sections.heading: How These Five Stack Up
paragraphs: The UPPAbaby Vista V3 is in a category of its own for families who want a single premium system that handles the newborn stage and converts to a double — the RumbleSeat II attachment adds a second child position while the main bassinet or seat stays in place. It's expensive, but if you're already a Vista family, the expansion path is seamless. The Baby Jogger City Mini GT2 Double is the best pure side-by-side: one-hand fold, excellent all-terrain performance, and it fits through 32-inch doorways at 29 inches wide.

The Joovy Caboose Too is the sleeper pick for newborn-plus-toddler families — the sit-or-stand rear platform is genuinely loved by older toddlers who don't always want to sit, and the front seat accepts most infant car seats. The Graco Ready2Grow LX is the budget tandem with more configuration options than anything else at its price, though the push quality and fold convenience reflect that lower price. The Zoe XL2 Best is the travel-specialist: lightest on this list, collapses to carry-on dimensions, and has an airline-gate-check bag included.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
paragraphs: Already own a Vista? Add the RumbleSeat and don't think twice. Starting fresh with a newborn and toddler? The Joovy Caboose Too handles that specific age gap better than any stroller on this list, at a reasonable price. For same-age twins or kids who'll both want to sit, the City Mini GT2 Double is worth the investment. Frequent flyers should seriously consider the Zoe XL2 Best as a dedicated travel stroller regardless of what they use at home.

faqs.q: Can I use a double stroller from birth?
faqs.a: Most double strollers accept an infant car seat in one position, which covers the newborn stage without a flat-lie seat. Full recline seats like the UPPAbaby RumbleSeat II are safe from birth. Always verify the specific recline angle and minimum age for each seat position.

Tandems are typically 20-24 inches wide and fit standard doorways. Side-by-sides range from 28-32 inches — check your doors and shopping aisles before buying. The Baby Jogger City Mini GT2 Double at 29 inches is the most doorway-friendly side-by-side on this list.

faqs.q: What is the weight limit for double strollers?
faqs.a: Most double strollers support 40-50 lbs per seat, for a combined limit of 80-100 lbs. The Graco Ready2Grow LX supports 50 lbs per seat. Check both per-seat and combined limits if you have older children.

faqs.q: Are double strollers allowed on airlines?
faqs.a: Most airlines allow a stroller as a free gate-checked item, but double strollers are often too large for overhead storage and must be checked at the gate or baggage claim. The Zoe XL2 Best collapses small enough to fit in overhead bins on some aircraft.

faqs.q: How long will I actually use a double stroller?
faqs.a: Most families use a double stroller heavily until the older child is about 4-5 years old, then occasionally until age 6-7 for longer outings. If your kids are less than 3 years apart, plan for 2-4 years of regular double use.

products.review: The Vista V3 is the most thoughtfully engineered double stroller system on the market — it starts as a single pram or seat stroller and expands to carry two children via the RumbleSeat II attachment without compromising the main seat. The MagnaMood canopy extends to near full coverage, the PiggyBack ride-along board adds a third option for an older child who wants to stand. It folds with both seats attached in a single motion. Yes, it costs more than some used cars, but it's also the last stroller most families will ever buy.
pros: Expands seamlessly from single to double without sacrificing main seat quality
One-step fold with seats attached — fits most mid-size SUV trunks
cons: Premium price is genuinely hard to stomach for a stroller
Combined weight of 40+ lbs when fully loaded limits portability

products.review: The City Mini GT2 Double is 29 inches wide — tight but passable through most 32-inch doorways — and folds flat with one hand while both seats are attached, which is a meaningfully rarer feature than it sounds. The all-terrain wheels and hand-actuated parking brake make it legitimately usable on gravel paths, not just marketing language for smooth-surface behavior. Both seats recline to near-flat independently and accept the Baby Jogger infant car seat adapter for newborns.
pros: One-hand fold with both seats attached — fast and genuinely useful
All-terrain wheels handle gravel, packed dirt, and grass well
Both seats recline independently to near-flat for different-aged children
cons: 29-inch width is tight for some doorways and grocery aisles
Heavier than the Zoe at 28 lbs before children are loaded

products.review: The Caboose Too's trick is the rear bench-seat that converts to a standing platform — older toddlers aged 2.5-5 who refuse to sit in a stroller will often happily stand on the back platform and hold the push bar. The front seat accepts most major infant car seat brands via adapter, covering the newborn stage. It's narrower than many tandems and handles single-door restaurants better than the Vista. The main limitation is that the rear seat is a simple bench, not a full recline seat, which matters for long nap-time walks.
pros: Rear sit-or-stand platform is a genuine differentiator for resistant toddlers
Accepts most major infant car seat brands in the front position
Narrower tandem profile fits through 28-inch doorways
cons: Rear seat is basic bench — no recline for napping older child
Front seat canopy doesn't cover both children in heavy rain

products.review: The Ready2Grow LX offers the most configuration flexibility at its price point — three riding positions for the second child including a standing platform, bench seat, and rear bucket seat. Both positions accept Graco infant car seats. It won't match the push quality or fold elegance of Baby Jogger or UPPAbaby, but for families who need a functional double on a budget and already own Graco car seats, the value is hard to argue with.
pros: Three rear riding configurations including stand, sit, and infant car seat
Accepts Graco SnugRide infant car seats in both positions
Budget price for a full-featured tandem with car seat compatibility
cons: Push quality noticeably below premium options on uneven ground
Fold is two-step and results in a large, unwieldy package for car trunks

products.review: The Zoe XL2 Best is 20 lbs — lighter than some single strollers — and folds to a bag that fits in most overhead storage bins on commercial aircraft. Both seats recline fully, include individual canopies with SPF50+ coverage, and support children up to 50 lbs each. The trade-off for the weight savings is smaller wheels that struggle on anything except smooth pavement, and a simpler frame that doesn't have the push confidence of heavier options. For urban families who take flights regularly, no other double comes close.
pros: 20 lbs is exceptionally light for a double stroller
Folds to carry-on dimensions for air travel — includes gate-check bag
Both seats fully recline independently with large SPF50+ canopies
cons: Small wheels struggle on gravel, grass, and uneven pavement
Frame flex under load feels less confidence-inspiring than heavier builds

pinDescription: The best double strollers of 2026 — tandem and side-by-side compared for real families. From newborn-plus-toddler to same-age twins, honest picks for every setup. 👶
